original_question: For k > 1, does the property Mix(k) lift under a typical extension, where typicality is understood in the Halmos metric?
target_in_paper: §1, Q7: "Does the property Mix(k), k>1, lift under a typical extension?"
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the property as Mix(k) with k>1, the extension setting, and the fact that typicality is meant in the Halmos-metric sense. It also stays on the exact open-problem track of §1 rather than drifting to a broader neighboring question.
missing_details: It does not quantify over a fixed base measure-preserving automorphism S; in context, the question is about extensions of a given automorphism.
It does not say explicitly that the ambient objects are measure-preserving automorphisms of a probability space.
It does not specify that the relevant extensions are skew-product extensions over the fixed base automorphism.

It does not make explicit that "lifts under a typical extension" means: among all extensions of S, the set of extensions having Mix(k) is generic/comeager in the extension space equipped with the Halmos metric.
It does not define Mix(k) itself, i.e. the k-fold mixing limit for measurable sets under mutually separating time shifts.
It does not clarify whether k is fixed in advance or whether one is asking for simultaneous preservation for all k>1; the paper’s formulation is the fixed-order property Mix(k), with k>1 arbitrary.
It does not distinguish the fixed-order property Mix(k) from the stronger global property of multiple mixing of all orders.
refined_question: Fix an integer k>1, and let S be a measure-preserving automorphism of a probability space that has the k-fold mixing property Mix(k), meaning that for all measurable sets A0, A1, ..., Ak one has μ(A0 ∩ S^{n1}A1 ∩ ... ∩ S^{nk}Ak) → ∏_{i=0}^k μ(Ai) whenever the time shifts separate pairwise. In the space Ext(S) of skew-product extensions of S, endowed with the Halmos metric, is the set of extensions R that also belong to Mix(k) generic (equivalently: is a typical extension of S again k-fold mixing)?
justification: The draft is targeting the open problem stated explicitly as Q7 in §1. The surrounding paragraph first recalls the known result that a typical extension, in the Halmos metric, of every mixing automorphism is again mixing, and then asks the corresponding higher-order question for Mix(k). The earlier lines of §1 introduce k-fold mixing and the notation Mix(k), so the paper-faithful sharpening is to quantify over a fixed base automorphism S with Mix(k) and ask whether Mix(k) is generic in its extension space. It would be broader than the paper to rewrite this as a conjecture about full multiple mixing of all orders at once.
